newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise on Africa Israel's surge.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise on Africa Israel's surge.

text.p: Israeli shares surged across the board on Wednesday following a sharp rise in Africa Israel Investments, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 4.77 points, or 2.73 percent, to 179.75 on an all-share turnover of 87 million shekels against 57 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 index rose 2.86 percent to 191.22.

"We were overwhelmed by the market's strength today. Everything was rising following the rise of Africa Israel. Nothing fundamental has changed but the whole market is rising," said Danniella Finn at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"It is very difficult to predict what the market will do tomorrow and if the positive momentum will continue. The crisis of the provident funds is not over yet but share prices are very cheap," she added.
Africa Israel soared the maximum 10 percent to 469,477. The share rose following reports that Bank Leumi started puchasing shares in its subsidiary. Bank Leumi owns 52 percent of Africa Israel.

A banking source said that Bank Leumi has started purchasing the shares to ensure a solid majority to see that the spin off of Migdal insurance from Africa Israel goes through. Italian insurer Generali Spa has offered to purchase Migdal.

On Tuesday Africa's share soared 10 percent on rumours that entrepreneurs Motti Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer were purchasing shares in the company in an attempt to stop the Migdal spin off by raising their stake in the company to 25 percent.
Press reports said that the two now hold nearly 16 percent of the company.
Africa's convertible bond, the most active share today, rose 5.5 percent to 121.0 on a very high turnover of 20 million shekels.

Koor Industries, the second most active share, rose 1.75 percent to 27,711 on volume of 5.2 million shekels after the company said that net profit in the second quarter of 1996 rose to 191 million shekels from 152 million in the same quarter in 1995. During the first half of the year net profit was 392 million shekels as against net profit of 339 million in the first six months of 1995. Traders said that Koor's earnings were above expectations.

Osem Investments lost 0.75 percent to 1,931 after it said that net profit in the second quarter fell to 11.4 million shekels from 13.2 million at the same quarter in 1995. During the first half of 1996 net profit fell to 32.2 million shekels from 33.6 million in the first six months of 1995.

"The rise of Africa Israel shows that the whole market is under-priced. The market was also reacting to the fact that the central bank bought foreign currency to support the basket and this is seen as a positive sign," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

On Tuesday the central bank intervened in foreign currency trading for the first time in six months. Traders said that from now on the dollar can only rise and this will be good for Israeli exporters.
"The market was also reacting to the rise of Israeli shares traded in New York and to a rise of the bond market," Nahum said.
Super-Sol rose 3.0 percent to 6,870 on turnover of 4.8 million shekels.
